skill.name: obsidian-plan-wiki
skill.description: Build and maintain Obsidian-compatible project plan wikis with linked markdown files, task comments, changelogs, and research records.
skill.summary: Create modular Obsidian plan wikis for project roadmaps, research notes, and task tracking.
skill.author: Cygnusfear

security_audit.summary: No confirmed malicious behavior was found. The static findings are false positives from markdown code fences, inline formatting, Obsidian relative wiki-links, a benign grep example, and Mermaid diagram syntax.

static_findings.snippet: 2. Add arrow \`→\` with link to result
- Working with existing plan wikis using `%% [ ] %%` task format
2. Add arrow `→` with link to result
Every change must be logged in `changelog.md` using Keep a Changelog format:
- Update task marker to `[x]` with result link
2. Use descriptive name: `topic-name.md` or `topic-delphi.md` for Delphi synthesis
4. **Preserve deferred work** - Never delete, move to `deferred.md`

content.value_statement: Complex project plans become hard to navigate when details live in one long file. This skill creates linked Obsidian markdown wikis with focused tasks, research notes, and changelog records.
actual_capabilities: Creates a modular markdown folder structure for project plans.
Defines README, changelog, phase, task, reference, and research file templates.
Uses Obsidian wiki-links for navigation between related plan files.
Tracks open questions with hidden Obsidian comment checkboxes.
Describes a research workflow for simple oracle checks and Delphi-style synthesis.
Maintains amendment history with a Keep a Changelog style format.
limitations: Does not include scripts that create files automatically.
Requires manual review of generated plans for project-specific accuracy.
Assumes users are comfortable with markdown and Obsidian wiki-links.
Research workflow quality depends on the available sources and user instructions.

use_cases.title: Plan a Software Roadmap
use_cases.description: Create linked phase and task files for a multi-stage software project.

use_cases.title: Organize Research Decisions
use_cases.description: Capture research questions, findings, and recommendations beside implementation tasks.

use_cases.title: Maintain Project Knowledge
use_cases.description: Keep plan changes, deferred work, and reference notes in a navigable Obsidian vault.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Plan Wiki
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian plan wiki for this project: [describe project]. Include README, changelog, phases, tasks, and research structure.

prompt_templates.title: Break a Roadmap Into Tasks
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn a rough roadmap into linked task files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this roadmap into an Obsidian plan wiki with phases, task files, open questions, and success criteria: [paste roadmap].

prompt_templates.title: Process Open Questions
prompt_templates.scenario: Review existing task comments and plan research.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this plan wiki and identify open Obsidian task comments. Recommend which questions need research and where results should be linked.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor an Existing Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced cleanup for a large plan wiki.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Obsidian plan wiki for navigation, task scope, research links, changelog coverage, and deferred work handling. Propose focused amendments.

output_examples.input: A founder needs a plan wiki for a mobile app launch.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a linked plan outline with phases, task pages, research placeholders, and a changelog entry for the initial structure.

output_examples.input: A team has open architecture questions in task comments.
output_examples.output: The skill groups the questions, recommends research paths, and shows where completed findings should be linked in the plan.

output_examples.input: An existing roadmap is too long for daily use.
output_examples.output: The skill splits the roadmap into focused phase and task notes while preserving navigation and amendment history.

best_practices: Keep each markdown file focused on one phase, task, research topic, or reference area.
Update the changelog immediately after each plan amendment.
Use clear Obsidian links so readers can move from overview to details quickly.
anti_patterns: Do not place the full project plan in one long README file.
Do not delete deferred work without recording the decision.
Do not mark research questions complete until the result is linked from the relevant task.

faq.question: Does this skill require Obsidian?
faq.answer: No. The files are markdown, but Obsidian improves navigation through wiki-links.

faq.question: Can it update an existing plan wiki?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review existing linked markdown files and suggest focused amendments.

faq.question: Does it run commands or scripts?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation-based and includes markdown templates only.

faq.question: How are open tasks tracked?
faq.answer: Open items use hidden Obsidian comment checkboxes that can be marked complete with a linked result.

faq.question: What research workflow does it support?
faq.answer: It supports single-question research and a Delphi-style pattern with multiple perspectives and synthesis.

faq.question: Is it suitable for non-software projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The structure works for any complex plan that benefits from phases, tasks, references, and research notes.
